title: Amélie
synopsis: A shy waitress at the Two Windmills, a tin box of childhood treasures, and a man in a glass house who has been waiting for someone to listen.

nodes.text: A bathroom tile shifts and a small treasure of a stranger's childhood falls into your hand.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Return it” back. Heart shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
“Keep it” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Curious.

nodes.text: A phone rings and a stranger answers a question he has been carrying for forty years.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Shy.

nodes.text: A glance at a stuck life and a passport in your hand.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Mischievous.
You commit to “Leave it.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Two cheeks and a forehead, and a moped pulling away from the curb, and a courtyard that has, finally, a sound of laughter in it.
You start a small museum of returned objects above your bed. People come to see it from across the arrondissement. You blush every time.
The Glass Man finishes the painting at last. He looks at it and laughs and cries and offers you a glass of milk. You take it.
